newsitem.title: USA: Police arrest third suspect in U.S. bomb plot.
newsitem.headline: Police arrest third suspect in U.S. bomb plot.

text.p: Police said on Monday they had arrested a third suspect in connection with a series of bombings but were still searching for a man suspected of ordering the attacks to disrupt his trial on drug charges.

Army Osotonu, 34, was arrested on Sunday and faces conspiracy and explosives charges, Vallejo police spokesman Bill Powell said. His brother, Oston Osotonu, 24, and Francis Ernestberg, 40, were arrested on Sunday on similar charges.
Police said they were still searching for alleged ringleader Kevin Robinson, 29, wanted on suspicion of conspiracy and explosives violations.
Powell said police were "trying to develop information" on a possible fifth suspect in the case.

Police said Ernestberg and Oston Osotonu were suspected of planting bombs that damaged a court and a bank in Vallejo, 35 miles (50 km) northeast of San Francisco, in the last 10 days. No one was injured in the pre-dawn blasts.
Police disarmed a third bomb containing at least 30 sticks of dynamite found on Jan. 25 outside a public library that also housed a police evidence room.

Vallejo police chief Robert Nichelini said authorities received a call on Monday morning from someone who said he might have contact with Robinson and would like to encourage him to surrender. "That as far as I know has not materialized. We have no idea where he is," Nichelini said.
Jackson said earlier that police were concentrating their search for Robinson in the Vallejo area. He said police considered Robinson "armed and dangerous".

Vallejo police spokesman Lt. Ron Jackson said police believed Robinson hired two men already in custody to carry out the bombings to disrupt his trial on drugs charges that was due to start in a nearby town on Monday.
"We think it was a bombing for hire," Jackson said.

Robinson faced trial on charges of possession of cocaine base for sale, Jackson said. Since he has previous convictions, a conviction on this charge could have brought Robinson a life prison term under California's "three strikes and you're out" law, police said.
"It's our opinion that he has conspired with these other individuals in an effort to do whatever he possibly can do to stop his trial from starting today," Nichelini told reporters.

Nichelini said police believed Robinson's intention was to "either destroy evidence that he thought would help him beat these charges or conversely to put fear into criminal justice system workers or stop the operations of the building or do something that would either delay or stop his trial."

On Sunday, police seized 500 lbs (230 kg) of dynamite stored in a Vallejo garage and found a car with 61 sticks of dynamite in the trunk that investigators believe the bombers had wired up ready for use in another attack.
Jackson said police believed they had now recovered all of the dynamite that had been stolen from a construction site.
Authorities say the Vallejo bombings are not connected to three mail bombs found in the San Diego area in recent days.
